detailed_rationale:
Aditya Vision is a multi-brand consumer-electronics and durables retail chain headquartered in Patna, historically anchored in Bihar/East India and expanding its footprint, offering 10,000+ products (digital gadgets, home appliances, entertainment, personal care) from brands including Samsung, LG, Sony, Godrej, Whirlpool, Haier and Lenovo. Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026 quarter) revenue was Rs 1,193 crore versus Rs 940 crore a year earlier, up ~27% YoY, with net profit of Rs 77.22 crore and operating margin stable at 9-10%. This growth rate is consistent with what was reported for Q3 FY26 (~28% YoY revenue growth on strong festive demand) - i.e., this is a multi-quarter, consistent growth pace rather than a single strong print, which is a meaningfully better growth-quality signal than a one-off spike.

The company continues to add stores as its primary growth lever (targeting 200+ operational locations, having added new stores each recent quarter), consistent with the quant data's strong growth scores (3yr 80.9, 1yr 66.7) built on a 3-year revenue CAGR of 26.4%. Return ratios are strong (ROE 24.5%, ROCE 20.7%) for a retail business, and the 10-year track record cited (27% sales CAGR, 59% profit CAGR) suggests a genuinely well-run regional retail consolidator rather than a recent flash of growth.

One item worth flagging for the record: promoter holding has declined from roughly 67.5% three years ago to 47.14% as of Jun-2026 - a substantial ~20 percentage point reduction. This is plausibly explained by capital raised (IPO/QIP-type issuance) to fund the aggressive store rollout, which is a normal and often value-accretive way to finance retail expansion capex and working capital, but the magnitude of the decline is large enough to note as a trend to monitor rather than dismiss outright. Consumer-electronics retail is a structurally thin-margin, competitive category (national chains, e-commerce players like Amazon/Flipkart, and other regional rivals), which caps how far margins can expand even as revenue scales - Aditya Vision's edge appears to be regional density and service/after-sales relationships in markets less penetrated by the national chains and e-commerce.
recommendation_rationale: Quant score is Hold. The consistent, multi-quarter growth trend and strong return ratios are genuinely attractive, but thin structural retail margins and a valuation that already reflects a successful growth-retail narrative (alongside the promoter-holding dilution trend worth monitoring) mean there is no basis to push beyond Hold; nothing points to distress that would argue for more caution.
summary: Aditya Vision, a Patna-based consumer-electronics retail chain, continues to grow consistently at around 27-28% per quarter across at least the last two quarters reported, supported by ongoing store additions and strong underlying return ratios. This multi-quarter consistency is a healthier growth signal than a single strong print. Margins remain thin and stable, typical of consumer-electronics retail, and promoter shareholding has declined meaningfully over the past three years, plausibly reflecting capital raised to fund store expansion - a trend worth watching rather than a current red flag.
positive_para: Growth has been consistent across multiple recent quarters (~27-28% YoY revenue growth reported in both the most recent and an earlier quarter this year), a healthier signal than a one-off spike, backed by strong return ratios (ROE 24.5%, ROCE 20.7%) and a long track record (10-year sales CAGR of 27%, profit CAGR of 59%) of successful regional retail execution and store-network expansion toward a 200+ store target.
negative_para: Consumer-electronics retail is structurally thin-margin (operating margin steady at just 9-10%) and intensely competitive against national retail chains and e-commerce platforms, capping how much profitability can scale even as revenue grows. Promoter shareholding has fallen from ~67.5% to 47.14% over three years - a substantial dilution trend, plausibly tied to funding store-expansion capital needs, but large enough to monitor for what it implies about ownership alignment and future capital-raising needs.
reverse_dcf_judgment: The stock's valuation reflects a successful, consistently-executing regional retail growth story; against a demonstrated multi-quarter ~27-28% growth pace and strong return ratios, this looks like a reasonably-priced growth compounder rather than an obvious bargain or an obviously overpriced name - the key swing factor is whether margins can hold as the chain scales past its current regional density into more competitive markets.
